rv.q: With carefully shaded line readings and nuanced singing, she makes it sound like she's spent lots of time with the score so she could emulate the emotions of the heroine, both shown and implied.
In all, this was Oropesa and Salsi's evening and one more win for the 2025-26 Metropolitan Opera season.
His attention to dynamics enlivened the vibrant, supple carpet of orchestral sound, an important factor in making this performance so moving.
This production is certainly for someone.

cn.t: Mixed reception for Michael Mayer's lavish production, with critics divided on its opulent aesthetic. Sopranos Lisette Oropesa, Ermonela Jaho, and Rosa Feola earn praise, though some find the staging overly garish and better suited to Act I than intimate scenes.
